video.title: Stop Guessing. Here’s How to Build What People Will Actually Pay For

summary: Chris Koerner demonstrates a 'validate before you build' workflow: he polls 100 US small business owners via PickFu on which website feature they'd pay for, then uses the Mocha vibe-coding app to build an appointment booking widget (BookFlow) in under 20 minutes. Appointment booking tied with chatbot for first place; ChatGPT analysis of the written responses suggests bundling booking, forms, price calculator and a chatbot layer, leading with scheduling in ads. Key takeaway: poll your target buyer first, mine the free-text answers with an LLM, then prototype quickly with AI and sell before fully building. Mocha is described as a 'friend of the pod' (promotional link).

speakers.name: Chris Koerner

ideas.name: Embeddable appointment booking widget (BookFlow), niche-rebrandable
ideas.one_liner: A white-label booking widget for small business websites, vibe-coded with Mocha and sold into specific verticals such as dog groomers.
ideas.business_model: Software sold to small businesses (pricing not stated; implied subscription/widget licence)
ideas.customer: Small business owners with websites (dog groomers, tree trimmers, home service businesses, tarot readers, etc.)
ideas.problem: Businesses need clients to see their calendar and book appointments without messy email back-and-forth.
ideas.offer: An embeddable widget where visitors pick a service, date and time and enter their details; branding, colours and name are easy to swap per industry.

pricing.notes: No price for the widget is given; only the demo's dog-grooming service prices (45, 75, 15 dollars) which are example content, not product pricing.

acquisition_channels.details: Suggests running ads to a specific industry, with the top-of-funnel ad pitching scheduling and the other modules shown once they are inside.

quote.text: the top of the funnel ad should always pitch scheduling. That's where the strongest pain point in is.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

ideas.delivery: Software built by Mocha from prompts; multi-tenant app hosted at bookflow.mocha.app with custom domain option. Swapping to a new niche reportedly takes one prompt.
unit_economics_claims: Build took about 5 minutes for first version and about 18-20 minutes for the full site and demo
Agency build quoted at 10,000 USD in the US or 5,000 USD overseas, taking weeks
ideas.startup_cost: Mocha 20 USD per month plus PickFu poll cost (hundreds of dollars, exact not stated)
ideas.time_to_first_revenue: not stated (no sales made in the video)

acquisition.how: Paid ads to a niche landing page are inbound and can be run and optimised largely by agents with occasional human approval.

onboarding.how: Self-serve signup and widget embed code can be fully software-driven; per-niche rebranding is a prompt.

delivery.how: The widget is software running unattended once built; fixes and new niches are done via prompts.

billing.how: Standard subscription billing (e.g. Stripe) is unattended.

support.how: AI support can answer most install and config questions, but bugs in vibe-coded software need human review.

uk_applicability.notes: Software works the same in the UK; need GDPR/UK data handling for bookings and PECR compliance for outbound. Competes with Calendly and similar tools.

risks: Crowded market with established free/cheap booking tools
Vibe-coded app quality, security and reliability are unproven
Demo only; no customers or willingness-to-pay validated beyond a poll
Poll answers are stated preference, not purchase behaviour

tactics.name: Poll your target buyer before building
steps: Pick a platform like PickFu and target e.g. 100 US small business owners
Ask 'what one feature does your business need most that you would be willing to pay for?'
Offer 5 concrete options and require a written explanation
Optionally poll only ~20 people to save money, or ask friends, Twitter, Reddit or Facebook groups for free

quote.text: What one website feature does your business need the most right now that you would be willing to pay for?
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Mine free-text poll answers with an LLM
steps: Paste the written responses and vote totals into ChatGPT
Ask 'what can I learn from this that will help me make money?'
Look for gaps between what people want and what they'd pay for, and for bundling signals

quote.text: I posted a survey to business owners asking what features they would pay to have on their website.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Ask the AI to rewrite your prompt
steps: Write a rough prompt for the vibe-coding tool
Ask ChatGPT to rewrite it better, and to ask you questions if needed
Paste the long prompt as an attachment into Mocha
Trade-off: longer prompts cost more credits but may need fewer iterations

quote.text: ask it what to ask it
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Lead with the strongest pain point in ads, upsell modules inside
steps: Run top-of-funnel ads pitching scheduling only
Once the customer is inside, show other modules (forms, calculator, chatbot)
Bundle forms rather than selling them alone
Target a single industry per campaign by swapping branding via one prompt

quote.text: the top of the funnel ad should always pitch scheduling.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Sell before you build
steps: Poll, prototype in minutes, then pitch the prototype
Scale scope back to one niche widget (e.g. dog groomers) for a working demo
Clone to other niches with one prompt

quote.text: Poll, build, launch. Sell it before you have it. Ready, fire, aim.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

warnings.warning: Being needed is not the same as being willing to pay; sell painkillers not vitamins.

quote.text: a lot of us need stuff all the time, but it doesn't mean that we're willing to pay for it.

quote.text: what people want the most and what people are willing to pay for are not always the same thing.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Ask the target buyer what they would pay for before building anything, instead of assuming demand.

quote.text: Most people go about starting a business all wrong.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: You can validate without an audience by renting one (PickFu) or using free communities, friends and family.

quote.text: Ask your friends and family, go to Twitter, go to Reddit, go to a Facebook group
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Free-text reasons in a poll are often more valuable than the vote count, especially when analysed by an LLM for pricing and bundling signals.
Bundle commodity features (contact forms) into the main product rather than selling them standalone, since buyers expect them to be free.
A feature perceived as hard to build (chatbot) can raise the perceived value of an entire bundle even if few need it.
Vibe-coding collapses prototype time from weeks and thousands of dollars to minutes, so speed to market becomes the advantage.

quote.text: You can have an idea at 9:00 a.m. and have a working product ready to sell by noon
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: White-label a single codebase for multiple verticals so one product can be tested across niches cheaply.
Execution matters more than watching; act on the information.

quote.text: this video is cool, but it's only cool in so far as you actually do something about it.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

evidence_quality.rationale: A live demo of a validation and build workflow, not a running business: no sales, customers or revenue; poll is from paid US panelists; the product is a prototype with unproven quality. Process details (times, tools, poll results) are first-hand and consistent.
evidence_quality.promotional_conflict: Mocha is a 'friend of the pod' with a link in the description; host denies PickFu sponsorship but recommends it.
